# Kubernetes

Plugin ID `kubernetes`. How dash reaches and reads the cluster.

The kubernetes plugin reads the cluster through informers: nodes, namespaces, workloads, pods,
events, certificates and External Secrets on the Cluster page (a pod's logs come from the
victorialogs plugin and its metrics from the prometheus plugin); the volumes, their fill and
growth with days-to-full, the etcd size and the age of the backup CronJobs you name on the
Storage page; and the apps behind HTTP routes on the Apps page. Without
a kubeconfig or an in-cluster ServiceAccount it is `unavailable`: its pages are hidden and dash
serves everything else. The flux and cnpg plugins read the cluster through it.

## What it shows

### Pages

| Page | Path |
|---|---|
| Kubernetes cluster | `/cluster` |

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Overview, KPI row (`overview.kpis`) | Nodes | `nodes` |
| Storage (`storage`) | Persistent volumes | `pvcs` |
| Storage (`storage`) | Backup jobs and the etcd database | `backups-etcd` |
| Apps (`apps.sources`) | The apps behind HTTP routes | `apps` |

### Contributions

It contributes attention items, KPIs and the topology.

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `kubernetes.cluster` | `ClusterData` | Nodes, namespaces, pods, workloads and certificates. |
| `kubernetes.storage` | `StorageData` | Volumes and backups. |
| `kubernetes.apps` | `AppsData` | The apps behind HTTP routes. |

### API routes

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/plugins/kubernetes/pods/{ns}/{name}` | The detail of one pod: containers, conditions, owner chain and events |

### Series

Chart series on `/api/v1/series`: `node.cpu`, `node.mem`, `pod.cpu`, `pod.mem`.

## Dependencies

A change to a plugin's settings restarts it and the plugins that require or use it.

- **Uses** [Prometheus-compatible](prometheus.md) when it runs.
- **Uses** [Gatus](gatus.md) when it runs.
- **Required by** [Flux](flux.md) and [CloudNativePG](cnpg.md).
- **Used by** [Proxmox VE](proxmox.md).

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.kubernetes` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginskubernetes), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.kubernetes.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.kubernetes.mode` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_MODE` | string | `auto` | no | no | How dash reaches the cluster: auto uses the kubeconfig when kubeconfig (or the standard KUBECONFIG variable) is set, else the in-cluster configuration, else runs without a cluster (the plugin is unavailable and the pages that need it are hidden); inCluster and kubeconfig insist on that one source and report an error when it is missing. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.kubeconfig` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_KUBECONFIG` | string | - | no | no | Path of a kubeconfig file, used outside the cluster (development). Empty means the in-cluster configuration. The standard KUBECONFIG variable fills it too; this setting's own variable wins. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.context` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_CONTEXT` | string | - | no | no | The kubeconfig context to use. Empty uses the kubeconfig's current context. Only read with a kubeconfig. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.qps` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_QPS` | integer | `20` | no | no | Requests per second dash's Kubernetes client may send. 0 or unset means the default, 20; a negative value is refused. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.burst` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_BURST` | integer | `40` | no | no | Burst of requests the client may send at once, at least qps. 0 or unset means the default, 40; a negative value is refused. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.etcd.job` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ETCD_JOB` | string | `etcd` | no | no | The job label of etcd's metrics in Prometheus. The default is etcd. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.optional.certificates` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_OPTIONAL_CERTIFICATES` | boolean | - | no | no | The cluster may lack the cert-manager CRDs: their absence is not a note. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.optional.externalSecrets` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_OPTIONAL_EXTERNAL_SECRETS` | boolean | - | no | no | The cluster may lack the external-secrets CRDs: their absence is not a note. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.optional.httpRoutes` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_OPTIONAL_HTTP_ROUTES` | boolean | - | no | no | The cluster may lack the Gateway API CRDs: their absence is not a note. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.conventions.protectedLabel` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_CONVENTIONS_PROTECTED_LABEL` | string | - | no | no | Namespace label (value "true") that makes a restart ask you to type the workload's name. Empty protects no namespace. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.conventions.tenantLabel` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_CONVENTIONS_TENANT_LABEL` | string | - | no | no | Namespace label that puts the namespace under Tenants; its value is the tenant. Empty turns the grouping off. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.conventions.appsFluxPrefix` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_CONVENTIONS_APPS_FLUX_PREFIX` | string | - | no | no | Namespaces applied by a Flux Kustomization whose name starts with this prefix are listed under Apps. Empty turns the grouping off. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.apps.gateways` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_GATEWAYS` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | Only routes whose spec.parentRefs name one of these gateways are apps, as [{namespace, name}]. A parent reference without a namespace means the route's own namespace. Empty accepts every HTTPRoute. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.apps.excludeNamespaces` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_EXCLUDE_NAMESPACES` | list of strings (JSON) | - | no | no | Namespaces whose routes and ingresses are never apps (typically dash's own). Empty skips nothing. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.apps.annotationPrefix` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_ANNOTATION_PREFIX` | string | `gethomepage.dev` | no | no | The annotation prefix an app's name, group, description and icon are read from: <prefix>/name, <prefix>/group, <prefix>/description and <prefix>/icon. A trailing / is ignored. The default is gethomepage.dev. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.apps.ingress` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_INGRESS` | boolean | - | no | no | Also read networking.k8s.io Ingresses: one app per rule host. Needs get, list and watch on ingresses in the cluster role; off by default. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.upstreamViaAPIServer` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_UPSTREAM_VIA_API_SERVER` | boolean | - | no | no | Send the requests of the other plugins to in-cluster service URLs (http://<service>.<namespace>.svc) through the API server's service proxy, with the Kubernetes credentials. For running dash on a laptop against a remote cluster (development); off by default. Applies to requests made after the plugin starts. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.actions.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ACTIONS_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | Offer the plugin's actions. Off by default: without it the actions are not mounted and the web UI does not show their buttons. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.actions.denyNamespaces` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ACTIONS_DENY_NAMESPACES` | list of strings (JSON) | - | no | no | Namespaces the plugin's actions refuse, whatever the role. A JSON list in the environment. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.actions.agents` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ACTIONS_AGENTS` | string | `approve` | no | no | What an AI agent's call of one of the plugin's action tools (MCP, a token with the mcp audience) does: deny hides the tools and refuses them, approve creates an approval request a person approves or denies in dash, allow runs the action at once. A target that needs its name typed (a protected namespace) always waits for a person's approval, even with allow. API tokens and signed-in people are never affected. The default is approve; applies live. |
| `plugins.kubernetes.backupJobs` | `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_BACKUP_JOBS` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | The CronJobs behind the backup ages, as [{namespace, cronjob, label}] (up to 8). cronjob also matches every CronJob named cronjob-<suffix>. label names the row; empty names each row after the CronJob. Empty hides the backup rows. A JSON list in the environment. |

- A failed discovery or a refused list of a group marked in `plugins.kubernetes.optional.*`
  still adds a note to its topic.
- `plugins.kubernetes.apps.gateways` in the environment:
  `DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_APPS_GATEWAYS='[{"namespace":"gateways","name":"main"}]'`.
- An app's `/icon` annotation is a dashboard-icons name, a same-origin path or a URL under
  `ui.iconBaseURL`.
- `plugins.kubernetes.apps.ingress` reads `networking.k8s.io/v1` Ingresses, one app per rule host
  (`https://<host>`), with the same annotations and exclusions as the routes.
- A `plugins.kubernetes.backupJobs` row shows the age of the last success of the CronJob, read
  from kube-state-metrics' `kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time` through the prometheus
  plugin. With a `label` the entry is one row of that name, aged by its freshest CronJob.

## Actions

### `restart`: Restart

`POST /api/v1/plugins/kubernetes/actions/restart`, for administrators. Destructive. Not idempotent. Confirmation: the web UI asks in a dialog.

Input, a JSON object: `kind` (string); `namespace` (string); `name` (string); `confirm` (string).

### Limits

- **Off by default.** The actions are mounted only while `plugins.kubernetes.actions.enabled` is `true` (`DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ACTIONS_ENABLED`); until then their routes answer 404 and the web UI shows no button for them. A change restarts the plugin.
- **Administrators only.** A viewer gets 403 `forbidden`.
- **Rate limit.** One user may start 10 actions a minute, across every plugin's actions; more answer 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.
- **Strict input.** The body is JSON with only the fields above; a missing required field or a value outside its list answers 400 `invalid_input`.
- **Denied namespaces.** `plugins.kubernetes.actions.denyNamespaces` (`DASH_PLUGINS_KUBERNETES_ACTIONS_DENY_NAMESPACES`) lists namespaces where the actions answer 403, whatever the role.
- **Audited.** Each run is written to the audit log before it runs and again with its outcome; when that record cannot be written the action is refused (503 `audit_unavailable`). The 403 and 429 refusals above are recorded as denials, at most one per user (or, before sign-in, per peer) and reason a minute; a 404 or a 400 `invalid_input` is not.
- **Guardrail.** On Kubernetes, the Helm chart's admission policy holds dash's ServiceAccount to exactly the write these actions make, whatever RBAC grants: see [the guardrail](../deploy/kubernetes.md#the-guardrail).

- `restart` is a rollout restart of a Deployment, StatefulSet or DaemonSet: it sets the pod
  template's `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation. `kind` is `Deployment`,
  `StatefulSet` or `DaemonSet`; `namespace` and `name` are DNS names.
- In a namespace that `plugins.kubernetes.conventions.protectedLabel` marks, the caller also
  types the workload's name (the `confirm` field).

## Kubernetes RBAC

dash reads the cluster with its ServiceAccount. The Helm chart grants each group of rules below while the value named is set ([RBAC modes](../deploy/kubernetes.md#rbac-modes)); with `rbac.create: false`, grant them yourself.

**To read the cluster** (chart: `rbac.read`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [nodes, namespaces, pods, persistentvolumeclaims, events]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [apps]
    resources: [deployments, statefulsets, daemonsets, replicasets]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [batch]
    resources: [jobs, cronjobs]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  # The CRDs the plugin reads when the cluster has them.
  - apiGroups: [cert-manager.io]
    resources: [certificates]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [external-secrets.io]
    resources: [externalsecrets]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
  - apiGroups: [gateway.networking.k8s.io]
    resources: [httproutes]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
```

**With `plugins.kubernetes.apps.ingress: true`** (chart: `config.plugins.kubernetes.apps.ingress`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [networking.k8s.io]
    resources: [ingresses]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
```

**With `plugins.kubernetes.actions.enabled` (the restart action)** (chart: `rbac.actions.restart`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  # The protected-label check reads the namespace first.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [namespaces]
    verbs: [get]
  # The pod template's restartedAt annotation.
  - apiGroups: [apps]
    resources: [deployments, statefulsets, daemonsets]
    verbs: [patch]
```

**For `k8s:` secret references** (chart: `rbac.secretRefs`), in a Role in each namespace:

```yaml
rules:
  # One name per Secret a k8s: reference names in this namespace.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [secrets]
    resourceNames: ["<name>"]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
```

**With `plugins.kubernetes.upstreamViaAPIServer` (development)** (the chart grants none), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  # A proxied GET is authorized as get, a proxied POST as create.
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [services/proxy]
    verbs: [get, create]
```

The kubernetes plugin's restart and the flux plugin's reconcile are dash's only writes to the
cluster (apart from the requests `upstreamViaAPIServer` proxies, a development setting), the
reconcile through the kubernetes plugin's client. Discovery and the version check use the
default `system:discovery` and `system:public-info-viewer` bindings.

A resource the API server serves but the ServiceAccount may not list (Ingresses, or the
certificates, ExternalSecrets or HTTPRoutes when their permission is missing) is published without
its objects after 60 seconds, and the row is `degraded` with `cannot list: <name> (<category>)`,
where `<name>` is `ingress`, `cert-manager`, `external-secrets` or `gateway-api`, for example
`cannot list: ingress (auth)`; the topic's source note carries the same category.

A mark in `plugins.kubernetes.optional.*` also keeps the row healthy when the discovery of that
group fails (an aggregated API that is down) or its resource cannot be listed; the topic's source
note still says so.

## Secrets from Kubernetes (k8s:)

Any secret field takes `k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key>`: the value of one key of a Kubernetes
Secret. The kubernetes plugin reads it, so the plugin must run (a cluster, and
`plugins.kubernetes` not disabled). It watches each Secret it is asked for with
`fieldSelector=metadata.name=<name>` and nothing else; it never lists Secrets, keeps no Secret
object and copies only the keys the configuration names.

```yaml
plugins:
  proxmox:
    url: https://pve.example.com:8006
    tokenID: dash@pve!dash
    tokenSecret: k8s:dash/proxmox#tokenSecret
```

`list` and `watch` are needed because a watch with a `metadata.name` selector is a `list` and a
`watch` request; `resourceNames` is what limits them to the named Secrets. With
`rbac.create: false`, create a Role and a RoleBinding for dash's ServiceAccount in each namespace
a reference names:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: {name: dash-secrets, namespace: dash}
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: [secrets]
    resourceNames: [proxmox]   # one entry per Secret a k8s: reference names here
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata: {name: dash-secrets, namespace: dash}
roleRef: {apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: Role, name: dash-secrets}
subjects:
  - {kind: ServiceAccount, name: dash, namespace: dash}
```

A plugin does not start while any `k8s:` reference in its section is unread, an optional
credential included (`auth.bearerToken` and `auth.basic.password` of the Prometheus,
Alertmanager, Gatus and VictoriaLogs sources too): it would otherwise query without the
credential. Its row says `waiting for a Kubernetes Secret (see plugins.<id>.<field>)` (once for
each such field), after `not configured: set plugins.<id>.<setting>` when something else is
missing too. Its state is `unconfigured` when its other settings are complete, otherwise
`disabled` (or `unconfigured` when `enabled: true`). The row never names the namespace, the
Secret, the key or the reason; dash's log does, once per change (`not_found`, `key_missing`,
`forbidden`, `unreachable`, `kubernetes_unavailable`).

The plugin starts by itself when the values arrive, and a rotated Secret applies to the next
request without a restart. A waiting plugin counts as settled for `/readyz`: a Secret that cannot
be read never keeps dash unready.

The value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, as an `env:` or `file:` value is (a Secret made
with `kubectl create secret --from-file` usually ends in a newline), and a blank value counts as
missing (`key_missing`). It is held in memory only: never written to disk, to the settings store,
to `core.plugins`, the stream or the log.

When the Secret is deleted, or the kubernetes plugin stops (a reload, a lost cluster), the last
value stays in use; only the reason the log shows changes, and the next successful read replaces
it. A reload that adds a `k8s:` reference to a running plugin restarts that plugin in-process: it
waits until the value is read, and dash itself needs no restart.

`dash config validate` checks the syntax of the reference and reads no Secret.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing. Its actions are mounted and change nothing outside dash.

The restart action answers 202 and changes nothing.
